subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
subtype: Approach: family meeting to share responsibilities [Action]
passage: On Sunday evening in Dublin, Freya opened a video call and held her list up to the camera. Her brother Gabriel was in his kitchen in Cork, and Aunt Maeve, their mother's sister, had a mug in her hands. "Mum needs about twelve hours of help a week," Freya said. "Hospital visits, bills, phone check-ins, sorting her tablets into the weekly box. I can't do all of it with my job." Gabriel spoke first. "I'll take the finances and drive her to the hospital." "And I'll do the daily calls and set up the tablet box," said Freya. Aunt Maeve added, "I'll go round on Saturdays for tea." They wrote it down and sent it round. Nobody said it was perfect, but everybody knew what was theirs.

qa.q: Which jobs did Gabriel say he would take?
qa.a: Gabriel said he would take the finances and drive their mother to the hospital.

qa.q: What was Freya feeling when she said "I can't do all of it with my job"?
qa.a: Freya felt stretched and worried about coping alone, though she was ready to ask for help clearly.

qa.q: What could the family do if Aunt Maeve's Saturdays become hard to keep?
qa.a: They could look at the list again after a month and move tasks around or add paid help, since it is a shared plan.

qa.q: How might Gabriel have felt being asked directly?
qa.a: Gabriel may have felt glad to have clear tasks he could do, rather than a vague worry about his mother.

grounding: Freya calls her brother and aunt, states the tasks and time needed, and each takes a share.
